newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission acts over Canada clipped oats dispute.
newsitem.headline: Commission acts over Canada clipped oats dispute.

text.p: The European Commission has decided to press ahead with a regulation on durum wheat imports even though its GATT dispute with Canada has not been resolved, an EU official said on Wednesday.

"Talks between the Commission and Canada over the issue of clipped oats have failed to resolve the issue and the Commission now feels that it is in breach of its GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) obligations," the official said.
European Union cereals experts will discuss on Thursday draft implementing regulations covering durum wheat imports under the GATT Article 24/6 agreement on EU enlargment.
Canada has been blocking progress because it says it wants to include quality criteria which would favour its own clipped oats exports.
"With the talks with Canada stalled the Commission has decided to introduce a regulation covering the annual 50,000 tonne quota for durum wheat for 1996/97.
"It is also proposing a regulation covering the half year from January 1 to June 30 which is the first period after the agreement was signed," the official said.
The Commission proposal omits the annual quota of 10,000 tonnes of clipped or processed oats covered by the Article 24/6 agreement.
The issue is listed for a vote at the EU's cereals management committee after the experts meeting.
The experts will also discuss an implementing regulation on Thursday covering an additional import quota of about 1,000 tonnes of millet.
"The quota is required under GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) rules covering the accession of Austria which traditionally imported about 1,000 tonnes of millet," the official said.
The item could be put to a vote at the cereals management committee.
The experts are also due to discuss on Thursday the quality standards to apply to wheat imported under the GATT minimum access agreement.

"The experts group will also set dates for inviting tenders for the import of 200,000 tonnes of soft wheat and 100,000 tonnes of durum wheat required under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade," the official said.
If a decision is reached by the experts group it may go to a vote in the cereals management committee afterwards.
